name: ring (BoringSSL-derived crypto primitives)
baseline: RustCrypto aes-gcm 0.11.1, p256 0.14.0 and rsa 0.10.0-rc.19 on x86_64; aes-gcm 0.10.3 on Apple M2
verdict_reason: An independent benchmark on a Ryzen 9 7940HS puts ring at 8.78 GiB/s for AES-256-GCM against 2.92 GiB/s for RustCrypto's aes-gcm, and far ahead on ECDSA P-256. A separate webrtc-rs A/B on an Apple M2 found ring 2.7x fewer cycles per packet than aes-gcm with its ARMv8 backend switched on. The 38x AES-GCM gap on the graviola M2 run is overstated: it used aes-gcm 0.10.3, whose ARMv8 AES path needed opt-in cfg flags, while the current aes crate detects ARMv8 AES at runtime on Linux and macOS.
tier_reason: Third-party benchmarks (graviola's author and the webrtc-rs project) with CPUs and crate versions stated; rustc version and flags are not shown for graviola.
claimed_speedup: Ryzen 9 7940HS: AES-256-GCM 8 KB 8.78 GiB/s vs 2.92 GiB/s (3.0x, derived from page data); ECDSA P-256 signing 81,642 vs 9,350.8 sigs/sec (8.7x, derived from page data); P-256 key agreement 24,490 vs 2,100.9 kx/sec. Apple M2, AES-256-GCM 1200 B seal+open x 100k: 74.2ms vs 157ms (aes-gcm with ARMv8 flags) and 1.87s (aes-gcm default build).
workload: graviola's criterion suite: AES-256-GCM encryption of 8 KB buffers, RSA-2048 and ECDSA P-256/P-384 signing and verification, X25519/P-256/P-384 key agreement. webrtc-rs: AES-256-GCM seal+open of a 1200-byte packet with a 12-byte AAD, 100,000 iterations.
hardware: Framework 16 laptop with AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS; MacBook Pro M2 (2022); Apple M2 (webrtc-rs)
os: Linux on the x86_64 laptop; macOS on the M2
platforms: Targets BoringSSL's C and assembly support (x86_64, aarch64 and others); needs a C compiler
one_liner: Rust API over BoringSSL's assembly: about 3x RustCrypto's AES-GCM throughput and 8x its ECDSA P-256 signing rate on a Ryzen 9 7940HS.
how_it_is_fast: The hot paths are BoringSSL's hand-tuned assembly: AES-GCM runs as one stitched pass that interleaves AES-NI/VAES encryption with carry-less-multiply GHASH, and the P-256 code uses dedicated field arithmetic. RustCrypto's aes-gcm makes separate AES and GHASH passes, which the webrtc-rs authors cite for the remaining 2.7x on ARM.
use_it_when: TLS or bulk AEAD where AES-GCM throughput matters
High-volume ECDSA P-256 or RSA signing and verification
skip_it_when: Pure-Rust builds without a C toolchain, or targets BoringSSL does not support
P-384-heavy workloads: aws-lc-rs signed 16,583 vs 3,358.7 per second on the same x86_64 laptop
caveats: The graviola page has no run date (served Last-Modified 2026-10-27) and no rustc version; benchmarking is described as non-automated on two laptops
The page marks ring's and aws-lc-rs's x86_64 AES-GCM results as using AVX-512; CPUs without AVX-512/VAES will see a smaller gap
The M2 rows use older RustCrypto releases (aes-gcm 0.10.3) than the x86_64 rows
tradeoffs: C and assembly from BoringSSL: needs a C compiler and inherits its side-channel limits
The README calls the project an experiment and repeats BoringSSL's warning against general use
